question.prompt: A triangular garden bed dug alongside a school fence has a base measuring 15 metres and a perpendicular height measuring 6 metres, exactly as shown in the diagram below. A landscaper needs to calculate the exact area of the garden bed before ordering mulch, remembering that a triangle covers exactly half (that is, divided by 2) of the rectangle sharing its base and height. What is the total area of the garden bed, in square metres?

visuals.altText: Triangle representing a garden bed with a base of 15 metres and a height of 6 metres.

question.explanation: The area of any triangle equals its base multiplied by its perpendicular height, with that result then halved. Multiplying the base of 15 metres by the height of 6 metres gives 90 square metres. Halving 90 square metres gives a final garden-bed area of 45 square metres. This halving step is essential, since a triangle always covers exactly half the area of the rectangle that shares its base and height.
